---
title: "R6. Correcting a published figure"
description: "Revisions and corrections, and what the policy asks of you."
---

Nothing in this playbook prevents an error reaching publication. What decides whether that error
damages trust is what happens next, and for official statistics NHSBSA has already written down
what happens next.

## What to do when a published figure has changed {#what-to-do-when-a-published-figure-has-changed}

The **NHSBSA Revisions and Corrections Policy** treats a revision and a correction as two different things. A revision is expected: statistics published as provisional and later finalised, a change of methodology, or the arrival of further data. A correction is an error.

{{< include /guidance/_partials/diagram-correcting-a-published-figure.qmd >}}

The policy grades errors by what they do to the conclusions, not by how big the number is. As an illustration, a small arithmetic slip that reverses a conclusion is significant. A large number restated without changing anything anyone decided is not significant.

The amendment is published alongside the link to the document. Where an error is known but corrected figures are not yet available, a note goes on the statistics. The note says so and makes clear the figures are subject to change.

### Who decides

The **Lead Official for Statistics** decides how to address an error in published statistics, consulting the National Statistician where appropriate. Who holds that post is recorded in the governance and management framework, and [who to ask](r3-who-to-ask.qmd) has the route to them.

### If your output is not official or national statistics {#if-your-output-is-not-official-statistics}

The policy does not bind it, and its behaviour is worth following anywhere. Say what was wrong, say what it changed, and say where the corrected version is. Leave the original visible rather than replacing it silently. An analysis that quietly acquires new numbers is indistinguishable from an analysis nobody checked.

## Where a correction connects to the rest of the playbook {#where-a-correction-connects}

A correction is a change to data, method or output after sign-off. From Level 3, the
[change control check](../07-deciding-your-assurance-level/what-your-level-requires.qmd#the-checks-by-level)
applies, and the change is re-assured proportionately.

What the correction shows about how the error got through is a lesson. That lesson belongs in
[Phase 5, review](../05-review/index.qmd).

[NHSBSA templates and documents](r2-templates-and-documents.qmd) lists the policy itself.
